title: Ensure 'Maximum password age' is set to '365 or fewer days, but not 0'
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 1.1.2: Ensure 'Maximum password age' is set to '365 or fewer days, but not 0'

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

parameters.name: max_password_age_days
parameters.description: Maximum allowed password age in days (must be > 0 and ≤ this value)

fields.name: password_age_days
fields.description: Actual maximum password age in days as detected on the target host

steps.name: Confirm domain controller and Group Policy tooling availability
steps.function: 1. Confirm the target is a domain controller and that Group Policy tooling is available. Run: `(Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole` and `Get-Module -ListAvailable GroupPolicy`. Expected result: DomainRole is 4 or 5 (domain controller), and the GroupPolicy module is listed. Both facts confirm the AD/GPO audit path is valid; if the host is not a domain controller or the module is absent, use the local policy fallback in step-03 through step-06.

steps.name: Check the 'Maximum password age' setting in the Default Domain Policy GPO
steps.function: 2. Check the 'Maximum password age' setting in the Default Domain Policy GPO using command: `Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy | Select-Object MaxPasswordAge`. Expected result: MaxPasswordAge is greater than 0 days and less than or equal to 365 days (e.g., 365.00:00:00 or less, but not 00:00:00 or unlimited).

steps.name: Check the 'Maximum password age' setting via the local security policy
steps.function: 3. Check the 'Maximum password age' setting via the local security policy using command: `net accounts`. Expected result: 'Maximum password age (days)' is a value between 1 and 365, not 'Unlimited' or 0.

steps.name: Check the 'Maximum password age' setting via secedit export
steps.function: 4. Check the 'Maximum password age' setting via secedit export using command: `secedit /export /cfg $env:TEMP\secpol.cfg; Get-Content $env:TEMP\secpol.cfg | Select-String 'MaximumPasswordAge'`. Expected result: MaximumPasswordAge is set to a value between 1 and 365.

steps.name: Check the 'Maximum password age' setting via registry
steps.function: 5. Check the 'Maximum password age' setting via registry using command: `Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netlogon\Parameters' -Name 'MaximumPasswordAge' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`. Expected result: MaximumPasswordAge is a value between 1 and 365, or the property is absent (indicating default domain policy applies).

steps.name: Check the 'Maximum password age' setting via auditpol or LGPO
steps.function: 6. Check the 'Maximum password age' setting via auditpol or LGPO using command: `LGPO.exe /parse /m $env:TEMP\secpol.cfg | Select-String 'MaximumPasswordAge'`. Expected result: MaximumPasswordAge is configured to a value between 1 and 365 days.

steps.name: Summarize overall compliance status: PASS if all checks confirm Maximum password age is set to 365 or fewer days but…
steps.function: 7. Summarize overall compliance status: PASS if all checks confirm Maximum password age is set to 365 or fewer days but not 0; SKIP if the Group Policy module or Active Directory environment is not present; FAIL if the setting exists but is configured to 0 (never expires) or greater than 365 days.

computations._cis_status: PASS if audit output contains '** PASS **', FAIL if '** FAIL **', SKIP otherwise

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).

The target is a domain server (domain controller). Audit the effective domain password policy via the Active Directory cmdlets (Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy) as the authoritative source; the secedit / net accounts / registry checks are corroborating fallbacks only, used when the GroupPolicy or ActiveDirectory module is unavailable. Only report SKIP when the host has no domain context at all (no AD module and DomainRole not 4 or 5) — do not SKIP merely because a local policy value is absent.
The maximum password age threshold is configurable via the input parameter max_password_age_days (default 180). All comparisons must use this parameter instead of a hardcoded 365.
The maximum password age threshold is fixed at 365 days. All comparisons must use 365 as the upper bound and 0 as the lower bound (exclusive).
reference_procedure: Navigate to the UI Path articulated in the Remediation section and confirm it is set as prescribed.
